title: Evaluation of a training programme on psychosocial issues for occupational physicians: a single-arm pre-post study with follow-up survey
summary:
Background: Psychological stress and mental illness are today among the most common reasons for absence from work. Occupational physicians talk to employees regularly. They can recognise psychological stress early, advise those affected and their managers, and help them find support. However, their training only partly teaches them the knowledge and conversation skills they need for this.
Research question: Ulm University Hospital has therefore developed a training programme with 70 teaching hours over ten days. The study examines whether the programme meets the needs of the participants, how their knowledge, conversation skills and attitudes change over the course of the programme, and whether they later use what they have learned in their everyday work.
Methods: Up to 36 occupational physicians take part in the programme in three rounds. At the beginning and at the end of the programme, they fill in a questionnaire, answer knowledge questions and hold practice conversations with actors. These conversations are recorded and later rated by members of the research team and by a person not involved in the programme, using rating sheets. In the first round, participants also give short anonymous feedback after each seminar day and talk about the programme in focus groups. Six months after the programme, all participants are asked online whether and how they use what they have learned in their everyday work. As there is no comparison group that doesn't participate in the programme, the study can merely describe changes. It cannot show with certainty that these changes are caused by the programme alone. The feedback from the first round is used to further develop the programme for the following rounds.
conditions: Mental health at work; competence of occupational physicians in prevention, early detection, counselling and referral of employees with mental strain or mental disorders.

interventions.name: All participants complete the training programme “Competence in psychosocial issues: an intensive training programme for occupational physicians”. The programme comprises ten seminar days (five two-day blocks, Friday and Saturday, each with 14 teaching units of 45 minutes; 70 teaching units in total

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
currently working as an occupational physician or as a physician in occupational health; participation in one cohort of the training programme; capacity to consent and written informed consent to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
participation in an earlier cohort of the training programme
